question.html:
One possible fission reaction of uranium-235 23592U is

23592U+n→13755Cs+9537Rb+4n

a Outline, with reference to the decay equation above, the role of chain reactions in the operation of a nuclear power station. [3]

The following data are given:

Binding energy per nucleon of 23592U    = 7.591 MeV

Binding energy per nucleon of caesium-137 13755Cs    = 8.389 MeV

Binding energy per nucleon of rubidium-95 9537Rb    = 8.460 MeV

b Calculate, in MeV, the energy released in the reaction. [2]

c

Two nuclides present in spent nuclear fuel 13755Cs are  and cerium-144 (14458Ce). The initial activity of a sample of pure 13755Cs is about 40 times greater than the activity of the same amount of pure 14458Ce.

Discuss which of the two nuclides is more likely to require long-term storage once removed from the reactor.
